nodes.speaker: Chief of Staff, Ana Reyes
nodes.text: Madam President, the inauguration crowd is waiting. Kastoria has not had a peaceful transfer of power in a generation, and every word you say today will be dissected. How do you want to open your address?

choices.text: Speak plainly to the people — promise to fight for them directly.
Speak carefully and technically — promise steady, competent governance.

nodes.text: Your first act in office: set the national budget priorities for the coming term. Adjust each ministry's share of spending.
Your cabinet awaits your first full meeting. Review the ministers who will carry out your agenda.

nodes.speaker: Finance Minister, Dorin Albescu
nodes.text: Madam President, the kastor has lost a third of its value overnight. Foreign reserves are draining fast. We need a decision within the hour.

choices.text: Impose emergency austerity — cut spending, raise taxes.
Print currency and launch a stimulus package.
Negotiate a careful IMF bridge loan.

nodes.speaker: Interior Minister, Yelena Kovak
nodes.text: The austerity measures have hit hard, Madam President. There are demonstrations forming in the capital, and they are growing by the hour.

choices.text: This will pass. Hold the course.
The streets are turning against us — this needs handling.

nodes.speaker: Defense Minister, Gen. Petar Milo
nodes.text: Inflation is climbing fast, Madam President. Some officers in the garrison are muttering about instability. I'd rather you hear it from me first.

choices.text: That sounds like a threat. Note it and move on.

nodes.speaker: Gen. Petar Milo
nodes.text: Madam President, the garrison commander is offering to clear the square by force before nightfall. He's waiting on your word.

nodes.speaker: Gen. Petar Milo
nodes.text: Border patrols report movement from Tavria across the Solen river, Madam President. It could be a drill. It could be worse. What are your orders?

nodes.speaker: Foreign Minister, Claudia Serban
nodes.text: The Halvorn Union has offered Kastoria a mutual defense pact, Madam President. The terms are generous — perhaps too generous.
A year has passed. Time to revise the national budget for the second half of your term.
Reshuffled or not, your cabinet meets to prepare for the final stretch before the election.

nodes.speaker: Ana Reyes
nodes.text: Election day is a week away, Madam President. The nation is watching your final address. How will you close out your term?

choices.text: An honest accounting — the good and the bad.
A triumphant victory lap, regardless of the numbers.

nodes.text: Kastoria goes to the polls, and the results are not close. Whatever the cost, the country has decided it trusts you with a second term. History will judge the rest.
The votes are counted, and Kastoria chooses a new path. You leave office having kept the republic intact, if not your own ambitions.
There is no real vote this time, only a formality. The garrison stands in the squares where the demonstrators once did. Kastoria is stable, and it is not free.
The kastor is worthless, the treasury is empty, and your government falls before the election ever takes place. Kastoria will remember your name, but not kindly.
